English.Text: All this walking in circles and for what, exactly?
The heat, the dust and the press of bodies is unbearable.
Months of travel just to stand around and wait.
They shuffle along endlessly, bumping into one another like cattle.
My feet ache just watching them.
Someone fainted again and no one even stopped.
The air is thick with sweat, dust, and exhaustion.
Left before it was finished, I could not stand the crowd.
A deeply unpleasant ordeal.
I've endured markets, sieges, and plagues, but this rivals them all.
No sense of direction, it’s just waves of people pushing forward.
Watching this feels like waiting for a queue that never ends.
If this is spiritual renewal, it comes at a steep price.
I've seen calmer crowds at the market.
Dust everywhere, and nowhere to sit.
No one seems quite sure where they're meant to go.
At least it's quieter than I expected.
A bit of shade would improve things considerably.
From above, it all blurs into one slow-moving mass.
I expected better organization for an event this large.
Some people seem more lost than inspired.
It all moves at a painfully slow pace.
Hard to feel uplifted when your feet hurt this much.
The food stalls are crowded and overpriced.
Security checks take longer than the prayers.
You can say you were there, at least.
Something about the crowd’s movement is oddly mesmerizing.
Not everyone knows where to go, but they seem determined enough.
Feels like the whole city showed up today.
Came out of curiosity, stayed longer than planned.
The view from the outer courtyard wasn’t bad.
You do end up talking to strangers without meaning to.
Heard languages I couldn’t even place.
Being closer makes the scale of it all clearer.
Everything seemed to run as expected.
The steady murmur never really stops.
No two groups seem to move quite the same way.
All in all, it went smoothly enough.
Everyone seems dressed for the occasion.
The flow of people is surprisingly calming to watch.
I’d come again, given the chance.
People of every age seem drawn here.
You can tell this means a great deal to many of them.
There’s a quiet intensity in the air.
Quite pleasant, all things considered.
It’s easy to find yourself quietly joining in.
There’s a certain grace to the way it all comes together.
The facilities are better than I expected.
The food nearby is simple, but satisfying.
You hear stories here you won’t hear anywhere else.
With so many people present, it’s impressively well managed.
A moment worth remembering.
Truly overwhelming. I will carry this moment forever.
Such grace, such unity, it feels almost unreal.
This alone was worth the entire journey.
No place on earth could have held this meaning.
I have never felt closer to something greater than myself.
Every hardship feels justified after this.
Faith made visible, standing right before us.
Body weary, spirit utterly full.
The moment it began, tears followed.
I doubt I will ever witness something like this again.
Every detail felt purposeful and sacred.
The atmosphere alone is enough to move the soul.
Not a single dry eye among us.
No one seems to know where they’re supposed to go, despite it's size.
You would think it such a small event would be better organized.
Neither that big nor that good.
A very low-key event.
Pretty average for that size.
I think the locals enjoyed themselves, anyway.
It’s modest, but there’s a quiet sense of purpose here.
A small gathering, yet everyone seems respectfully engaged.
What memories to treasure, every step felt meaningful.
Humble in scale, yet deeply moving and unforgettable.
Overcrowded, exhausting, and badly managed from start to finish.
All you hear are complaints echoing through the courtyards.
Too crowded to be comfortable, yet somehow lacking direction.
Many pilgrims look tired and frustrated rather than uplifted.
Well attended and orderly enough, though nothing extraordinary.
Moments of reflection balanced by long stretches of waiting.
A moving moment that lifted the spirits of the entire gathering.
The rhythm of prayer and movement felt calm and reassuring.
A profound gathering that left everyone visibly moved.
The shared devotion created an atmosphere of awe and unity.
A colossal waste of hype. Nothing lived up to the billing.
Tens of thousands turned up, and left wondering why they bothered.
So many pilgrims gathered, yet the journey felt oddly hollow.
The scale was immense, but the spirit never truly lifted.
Plenty of noise, plenty of effort, but not much else.
A solid spectacle, even if it never quite caught fire.
So many souls walking as one, on a journey, that finally feels worth the effort.
The chants, the candles, this is a gathering to remember.
This will be spoken of for generations, a pilgrimage that changed those who walked it.
In this vast gathering, faith feels boundless and the world briefly stands still.
